title: security eng sync notes - 2026-03-12
body:
Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh, Daniel Park, Monica Reyes, + oncall rotation

Agenda:
- Quick oncall / pager review
- Vulnerability triage highlights
- Secrets leakage follow-up and mitigation plan
- Threat model review: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem)
- Action items and next steps

1) Oncall / Pager recap
- No major production incidents this week. Two low-severity alerts: intermittent auth failures in eu-west region (investigating routing rule).
- Follow-ups: Daniel to confirm whether the auth failures correlate with recent routing policy change (due 2026-03-14).

2) Vulnerability triage (summary)
- SEC-479: Dependency vuln in `grpc-proto` flagged by SCA (high severity by score, exploitable in specific code paths).
  - Status: triaged -> remediation path agreed: upgrade to patched version 1.13.2 and add targeted unit test to exercise the parsing path.
  - Owner: Priya (PR opened, ref link in linked_artifacts). Target deploy to staging 2026-03-16.
- SEC-482: Privilege escalation report from fuzzing harness on runtime image builder. Repro steps partially deterministic.
  - Status: investigation. Liam to reproduce locally and narrow the exploit surface (sandboxing + file perms).
  - Temporary mitigation: restrict builder to dedicated service account with least privilege; enforce ephemeral builders.
- Notes: emphasize adding these two findings to the monthly risk register; Monica to add entry and notify compliance.

3) Secrets leakage follow-up
- Incident: Test repo contained a short-lived API key used in an integration test; surfaced by internal audit. Key was rotated within 2 hours; no external use detected.
- Root cause: missing enforcement of git-secrets pre-commit in one developer CI image + an overlooked service account token used in ephemeral CI job.
- Immediate actions taken:
  - Key rotated and access reviewed (completed).
  - Revoked related service account tokens and reissued with narrower scope (completed).
- Planned changes (owners/dates):
  - Enforce git-secrets and pre-commit hooks in all CI images and dev VMs (Owner: Priya, due 2026-03-19).
  - Add server-side scanning for secrets at push time (pre-receive hook) + block pushes with high-confidence leaks (Owner: Daniel, PoC due 2026-03-20).
  - Update onboarding checklist to include secrets scanning and KMS integration for dev creds (Owner: Monica, due 2026-03-26).
  - Audit of all long-lived tokens across org (Owner: Aisha + Security Ops, due 2026-03-24).
- Longer-term: Explore ephemeral credential patterns for CI (short-lived tokens via CI role assumption). Prioritize for Q2 roadmap if PoC is successful.

4) Threat modeling: Private deployment (VPC / on-prem)
- Context: Product team planning two pilot customers for private deployment later this quarter. We reviewed the proposed network and runtime architecture (per Confluence diagram).
- Key threat surfaces discussed:
  - Network egress path & data exfiltration: ensure default-deny egress controls and allow-list endpoints for telemetery.
  - KMS/HSM integration: customer-managed keys for model/data encryption; define key rotation and auditability requirements.
  - Lateral movement between tenant workloads: enforce strong tenant isolation; prefer separate namespaces/VMs rather than multi-tenant containers for early pilots.
  - Supply-chain risk for private package installs: mandate SBOM for any third-party packages included in on-prem bundles.
  - Side-channel concerns for shared GPU: recommend dedicated GPU allocation for private pilot customers, document risk and mitigations.
- Decisions / recommendations:
  - For pilot customers, require dedicated VPC + private networking with explicit egress rules. Engineering to provide hardened reference architecture and a checklist for customers (Owner: Liam, deliverable 2026-03-26).
  - Integrate with customer KMS when available; fallback to Redwood-managed KMS only with explicit contract and audit controls. Product/Legal to finalize contract language.
  - Threat modeling follow-up: schedule focused session with infra and product security to map data flows (Owner: Priya, meeting scheduled 2026-03-17).

5) Action items (clear owners + dates)
- Priya: Upgrade grpc-proto and open PR + tests (target staging deploy 2026-03-16).
- Liam: Reproduce SEC-482 locally and propose sandboxing mitigation (update by 2026-03-18).
- Daniel: Implement PoC pre-receive secret scanning and CI image enforcement (PoC 2026-03-20).
- Monica: Add vuln entries to monthly risk register & update onboarding checklist for secrets (2026-03-19 and 2026-03-26).
- Aisha + Security Ops: Org-wide token audit (report due 2026-03-24).
- Liam: Reference architecture + customer checklist for private deployments (deliverable 2026-03-26).

Open questions / parking lot:
- How strict should egress allow-listing be for pilots vs. production customers? (Product/Customer Success input required)
- Contract language for KMS fallback: legal to propose phrasing; need risk acceptance flow.
- Decide on default enforcement policy for ephemeral builders across all teams (ops trade-off vs. developer productivity).

Next meeting: Weekly security engineering sync -> 2026-03-19 10:00 PT

Notes & references:
- See Confluence page for architecture diagrams: /security/weekly-sync/2026-03-12
- Jira tickets referenced: SEC-479 (grpc-proto), SEC-482 (builder privilege).
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2145 (dependency upgrade PR by Priya)

End of notes.
